rationale: Both follow the required subclassing and delegation models correctly, with clean counters and properties. A also overrides readline, so direct readline() calls are metered as well, and __next__ is built on that metered readline. Every read path therefore goes through one counting mechanism, which is more complete and robust for a billing wrapper. B meters only read() and iteration: it calls super().readline() inside __next__ and leaves direct readline() calls unmetered. That is an inconsistency beyond what the tests cover. B's more descriptive local names (data, written, sent) are a minor plus, but A's more thorough instrumentation makes it the better design.
